skill.name: regulatory-affairs-head
skill.description: Regulatory affairs guidance for HealthTech and MedTech teams. It supports regulatory strategy, submission planning, pathway analysis, compliance coordination, and status tracking.
skill.summary: Guides medical device regulatory strategy, submission planning, and compliance coordination.

security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, network activity, or shell command execution. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, inline filenames, and regulatory prose. The only confirmed issue is a local JSON write in the tracker script, which should be constrained and documented.

remediation.issue: Local file write in tracker script
remediation.suggestion: Constrain data_file to a safe workspace path, reject absolute paths, and warn before overwriting existing files.
Document that regulatory_submissions.json may contain confidential submission data and should not be committed or shared.

content.value_statement: Regulatory teams need structured guidance for submissions, pathways, and compliance planning. This skill helps plan FDA, EU MDR, and global regulatory work.
actual_capabilities: Guides FDA pathway selection across 510(k), PMA, and De Novo routes.
Summarizes EU MDR planning tasks, evidence needs, Notified Body engagement, and post-market obligations.
Defines regulatory decision steps for impact assessment, stakeholder alignment, implementation, and monitoring.
Provides a local submission tracker script for status reporting and overdue item review.
Frames regulatory KPIs, risk controls, and cross-functional communication practices.
limitations: It does not provide legal advice or replace qualified regulatory counsel.
It does not verify current FDA, EU, or ISO rules from live authority sources.
Several resources named in SKILL.md are not included in the package.
The tracker script stores data locally and does not integrate with regulatory systems.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Device Submission Strategy
use_cases.description: Map likely FDA or EU MDR routes, evidence needs, timeline risks, and review milestones.

use_cases.title: Plan Market Access for a New Product
use_cases.description: Translate product scope, target markets, and quality readiness into a practical regulatory work plan.

use_cases.title: Track Submission Status and Escalations
use_cases.description: Use structured status reporting to identify overdue submissions, active reviews, and follow-up actions.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Submission Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this medical device and recommend a likely FDA or EU MDR pathway. Include assumptions, required evidence, risks, and next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Submission Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a regulatory submission plan for this product and market. Include milestones, owners, documentation needs, dependencies, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Review Readiness Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this submission readiness summary. Identify missing evidence, quality system gaps, authority questions, and cross-functional decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Global Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a global regulatory strategy for this device portfolio. Compare markets, sequence submissions, define risks, and propose governance metrics.

output_examples.input: A startup asks whether a connected diagnostic device should target FDA 510(k) or De Novo first.
output: A pathway comparison with assumptions about predicates and intended use.
A list of evidence gaps for software, clinical performance, labeling, and cybersecurity.
A recommended next step for pre-submission consultation.

output_examples.input: A regulatory leader needs a status report for active submissions and overdue milestones.
output: A concise status summary grouped by review stage.
A list of overdue items with responsible owners and target dates.
Escalation actions for authority questions and missing documentation.

output_examples.input: A team preparing EU MDR documentation needs common risk areas before Notified Body review.
output: A readiness checklist covering clinical evidence, PMS planning, risk management, and documentation traceability.
Likely review questions and recommended evidence owners.
A practical timeline risk summary for leadership.

best_practices: Provide product type, intended use, target market, risk class, and current evidence status.
Ask for assumptions and citations when decisions depend on changing regulatory guidance.
Review outputs with regulatory counsel or qualified affairs specialists before external use.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the skill as legal advice or final authority approval guidance.
Do not paste confidential submission data unless your environment permits it.
Do not rely on missing packaged references without verifying the source material.

faq.question: What regulatory areas does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on medical device submissions, FDA pathways, EU MDR planning, quality readiness, and regulatory coordination.

faq.question: Can it replace a regulatory affairs professional?
faq.answer: No. It supports planning and drafting, but qualified professionals must review decisions and official submissions.

faq.question: Does it check live regulatory updates?
faq.answer: No. It uses packaged guidance and should be paired with current authority sources.

faq.question: What tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the tracker send data over the network?
faq.answer: No evidence of network activity was found. The included tracker reads and writes local JSON data.

faq.question: What should users prepare before prompting?
faq.answer: Prepare product details, intended use, target markets, evidence status, quality system context, and timeline constraints.
